RoboParty opens RP1 hardware designs and motion-development resources

The release links mechanical files, electronics, simulation models and learning tools, with component-specific scope and licenses.

Humanoids Daily ↗15 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

From a demo to development files

RoboParty released a development stack for RP1, also called ROBOTO 01. Its GitHub hub connects mechanical and electronic designs, firmware, robot models and motion-learning tools. The material development is access for inspection and modification after the earlier IROS demonstration.

Tracing errors across layers

The hardware repository provides STEP models, PCB manufacturing files, wiring-harness information and configuration-specific bills of materials. MimicLite lists motion-policy checkpoints for 24- and 28-degree-of-freedom RP1 variants. Access across layers can help investigate whether an error comes from a policy, actuator or structure.

Check each component

Contents and licenses differ by repository: ROMOMO emphasizes joint documentation, while related code is maintained separately. The cited MimicLite comparison plot uses a Unitree G1 and is not an RP1 measurement. No retail price or delivery date is disclosed, and file availability does not establish independent reproduction of performance.
